claims.content: Enable the System Administrator to assign and modify staff access permissions, including security levels and passwords, for defined staff members.

goal.raw_text: Enable the System Administrator to assign and modify staff access permissions, including security levels and passwords, for defined staff members.

claims.content: System Administrator
The user must have System Administrative privileges to access the Configuration option.
Staff members must be defined in the system before security levels and passwords can be assigned to them.
For changes to device command rules on the production system, the System Administrator must first test the rule changes in the Simulator environment.
The System Administrator selects the 'Configuration' option from the GUI to assign or modify staff access permissions.

trigger.raw_text: The System Administrator selects the 'Configuration' option from the GUI to assign or modify staff access permissions.

claims.content: The System Administrator accesses the Configuration option via the GUI.
The System Administrator selects a defined staff member to configure.
The System Administrator assigns a security level and password to the selected staff member.
The System Administrator specifies the command level, device, mode, workstation, and system function for the assigned security level.
The System Administrator may modify user accounts remotely in field units if required.
The GUI analyzes the data before storing it in the database and notifies the System Administrator of any conflicting or redundant entries.
The system stores the Personnel Security Level entity with attributes: Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, and System Functions.

If the System Administrator enters conflicting or redundant entries while configuring staff access permissions, the GUI analyzes the data before storing it and notifies the administrator of the conflict.

If the System Administrator attempts to change device command rules on the production system without first testing them in the Simulator environment, the change is not permitted; the administrator must upload a new database version only after successful simulator testing.
The Personnel Security Level entity is stored in the database with the assigned attributes: Command Level, Device, Mode, Workstation, and System Functions.
The security level and password are assigned to the defined staff member.
User accounts may be updated remotely in field units if required.
